electronic-silicon-crystal-growth.text: Bulk resistivity is approximately the reciprocal of elementary charge times the sum of electron mobility–density and hole mobility–density products.

wafer-finishing-geometry.text: Usable circular area is pi times wafer radius minus edge exclusion, squared.
wafer-finishing-geometry.note: Requires 0 ≤ e < R. This is area, not a count of rectangular dies.

variables.meaning: Substrate lattice parameter in the same convention

epitaxial-material-stack.text: Lattice mismatch is film lattice parameter minus substrate lattice parameter, divided by substrate lattice parameter.

variables.meaning: Time-integrated ambient exposure, not adsorbed surface dose
Ambient concentration of the selected contaminant
Start and end of the exposure interval

contamination-and-surface-state.text: Ambient exposure is concentration integrated over the stated time interval.
contamination-and-surface-state.note: Choose a concentration unit such as particles/m³ or a mole fraction before assigning a numerical exposure. Adsorbed surface dose is a different quantity.

variables.meaning: Joint availability of all required services
Set of services required for the path
Event that required service i is available in the chosen scheduled-time population

cleanroom-subfab-utilities.text: Path availability is the probability that every required service is available together.
cleanroom-subfab-utilities.note: The intersection formalizes the original “all required services” event. Multiplying separate availabilities additionally requires independence, which is not assumed here.

variables.meaning: Incoming gas throughput in pressure–volume units
Effective pumping speed at the chamber

process-chamber-control.text: Chamber volume times pressure-change rate equals incoming gas throughput minus effective pumping speed times chamber pressure.

variables.meaning: Position in the package coordinate system

wafer-handling-genealogy.text: A package-coordinate position is the documented rotation or reflection of its wafer-coordinate position plus the translation.

variables.meaning: Material in process after the interval
Material in process before the interval

manufacturing-execution-dispatch.text: Next work in process equals current work in process plus arrivals minus departures, all in the same material unit.

variables.meaning: Oxidation time in the selected regime
Equivalent time accounting for initial oxide

thermal-oxidation-interface.text: Oxide thickness squared plus the linear length coefficient times thickness equals the parabolic rate coefficient times elapsed time plus equivalent initial-oxide time.

variables.meaning: Film thickness at the selected feature bottom
Film thickness at its defined top reference

cvd-pvd-film-transport.text: Bottom coverage is bottom-film thickness divided by top-reference thickness for the same feature.

variables.meaning: Film thickness in the established growth regime

ald-self-limiting-growth.text: Steady-regime thickness is approximately growth per cycle times applied cycles minus the effective nucleation-delay count.
ald-self-limiting-growth.note: Use only in the calibrated growth regime with N ≥ N₀; the expression is not a negative-thickness prediction before nucleation.

variables.meaning: Critical dimension after etch at the matched feature definition

resist-track-development.text: Transfer bias is after-etch critical dimension minus after-develop critical dimension at corresponding features.

variables.meaning: Declared relative importance of edge sample i
Predicted position of edge sample i
Target position for that edge sample

mask-opc-layout.text: The illustrative edge-error objective sums each squared predicted-minus-target edge displacement weighted by that sample’s declared importance.

variables.meaning: Depth of focus under the selected definition

lithography-resolution-focus.text: Resolution scales with wavelength divided by numerical aperture. Depth of focus scales with wavelength divided by numerical aperture squared, each with its own process factor.

plasma-wet-etch-transfer.text: Mask thickness consumed is approximately target etched depth divided by target-to-mask selectivity.

implantation-anneal-diffusion.text: The one-dimensional diffusion length scale is approximately the square root of twice diffusion coefficient times time.

variables.meaning: Empirical Preston coefficient for these units

clean-planarize-surface.text: The local empirical removal model multiplies the Preston coefficient, pressure and relative speed.

variables.meaning: Junction capacitance in the depletion approximation

wells-isolation-integration.text: Junction capacitance is approximately permittivity times area divided by depletion width.

fin-formation-integration.text: Effective gated width is approximately fin count times twice exposed height plus top width.

variables.meaning: Channel-material thickness lost in the toy selectivity budget

nanosheet-gate-last-integration.text: Channel thickness loss is approximately sacrificial removal distance divided by sacrificial-to-channel selectivity.

variables.meaning: One contact resistance under uniform injection

source-drain-contact-integration.text: Contact resistance is approximately specific contact resistivity divided by area. The complete path also includes channel, access-region and combined contact resistance.

variables.meaning: Total DC series resistance along the chosen path
Resistance of series wire segment i

beol-damascene-vias.text: Series-path resistance is the sum of wire-segment resistances plus via resistances.

interconnect-rc-materials.text: Wire resistance is resistivity times length divided by area. Distributed-RC delay scales with per-length resistance and capacitance times length squared.

variables.meaning: Voltage excursion under the declared current/path sign convention

backside-power-dtco.text: First-order supply excursion is approximately resistive drop plus inductance times current slew rate.

fab-metrology-process-window.text: Observed variance is the sum of process variance and independent additive measurement-error variance.

variables.meaning: Survival probability under the fatal-defect model

yield-wafer-defect-model.text: Independent Poisson fatal-defect survival is the exponential of minus defect density times effective die area.

variables.meaning: Residual defect probability among passing dies
Incoming probability of the defined defect
Detection probability conditional on that defect

known-good-die-test.text: Residual defect probability after a pass is incoming defect probability times the missed-detection fraction, divided by total pass probability.
known-good-die-test.note: Requires pass probability 1 − pc > 0. It assumes no false rejection of defect-free dies and one defined defect population.

variables.meaning: Stable throughput through the same boundary
Mean cycle time through that boundary

fab-ramp-cycle-time.text: For stable flow, average work in process equals throughput times mean cycle time.

variables.meaning: Idealized route-track count on one layer

flip-chip-abf-substrate.text: A single-layer geometric track estimate divides available routing width by track pitch.

rdl-fanout-integration.text: For independent zero-mean alignment contributions, the combined squared error is approximately the sum of their squared contributions.

variables.meaning: Packages supportable during the selected interval
Assembly starts possible during the same interval

cowos-s-silicon-interposer.text: Supported packages are bounded by the smallest compatible input stream after logic and HBM counts are converted to packages, and by assembly capacity over the same interval.

variables.meaning: Total dense-routing area counted without overlap
Package area using the same footprint convention

cowos-r-l-routing.text: Dense-routing area is the sum of its local regions. Dividing by package area gives the footprint fraction.

variables.meaning: Probability all required modeled connections survive
Failure probability of each independent connection

emib-local-bridge.text: All-link survival is approximately one minus per-link failure probability raised to the number of independent required connections.

variables.meaning: Probability an unscreened matched die pair is good before bonding
Events that the respective matched die is good
Marginal good-die probabilities for those sites

soic-foveros-vertical-routes.text: Unscreened pair yield is the joint probability that top and bottom dies are good; it factors into the two marginal yields only when their outcomes are independent.

bump-thermocompression-assembly.text: Uniform current density is joint current divided by conducting cross-sectional area.

variables.meaning: Geometric overlap of equal square pads

hybrid-bond-surface-alignment.text: Square-pad overlap is width minus the absolute horizontal offset, floored at zero, times width minus the absolute vertical offset, floored at zero.

temporary-carrier-thinning.text: Plate bending stiffness is Young’s modulus times thickness cubed divided by twelve times one minus Poisson ratio squared.

variables.meaning: Linear expansion coefficients of the two materials

package-thermomechanical-reliability.text: Free mismatch strain is approximately the difference between expansion coefficients times temperature change.

dram-cell-array-fabrication.text: Initial bit-line perturbation is approximately the cell share of combined capacitance times the initial cell-to-precharge voltage difference.

variables.meaning: Conducting via radius in the toy geometry
Radial keep-out distance beyond that radius

hbm-tsv-reveal.text: Via resistance is approximately resistivity times length divided by circular conductor area. The toy exclusion area uses a radius enlarged by the keep-out distance.

variables.meaning: Conditional survival of the incoming population at new stage i

hbm-stack-assembly-test.text: Expected output equals complete screened input sets times each successive stage’s conditional survival fraction.
hbm-stack-assembly-test.note: The y_i values are conditional on reaching each stage. The chain product does not itself require unconditional stage independence, but double-counted losses or unmodeled rework invalidate this simple path.

variables.meaning: Unit interval of the selected data-lane transfer convention
Effective transfers per second on one data lane

hbm-base-phy-controller.text: Unit interval is the reciprocal of the lane transfer rate. Timing margin is approximately that interval minus uncertainty and the required receiver window.

variables.meaning: Useful payload fraction under the declared workload

hbm-channel-generation-ras.text: Raw interface bandwidth is parallel data width times effective transfer rate divided by eight. Useful bandwidth multiplies that rate by the declared efficiency.

variables.meaning: Wafer requirement under the selected alternative model
Gross silicon area per bit under the geometric convention
Explicit nonoverlapping survival fraction excluded from a_bit
Empirical wafer requirement per delivered output bit

hbm-silicon-intensity.text: The geometric model divides target bits times gross area per bit by usable wafer area and an explicitly separate survival fraction. The alternative empirical model multiplies target output bits by measured wafers per output bit.
hbm-silicon-intensity.note: These are alternative models. An empirical output-bit intensity may already include yield; do not add the same loss again.

variables.meaning: Clock rate under the stated timing assumption

cpu-out-of-order.text: Execution time cannot be shorter than dependency-critical path cycles divided by clock rate.

variables.meaning: Useful elements processed, greater than zero

cpu-vector-matrix.text: Tail-packing utilization is useful elements divided by vector width times the number of vector instructions rounded up.

variables.meaning: Mean access latency in the two-path model

coherence-numa.text: Mean latency is the local-access fraction times local latency plus the remaining fraction times remote latency.

variables.meaning: Active lanes in issued instruction i
Issued lane slots available in instruction i

simt-active-lanes.text: Masked-execution efficiency divides all active lane participations by all issued lane slots over the same instructions.
simt-active-lanes.note: The introduced a_i and s_i explicitly name the original active_lanes and issued_lane_slots quantities. The denominator must be nonzero.

gpu-occupancy-pipeline.text: With ideal overlap, steady tile time is at least the larger of per-tile load time and compute time.

variables.meaning: Minimum time demanded by the selected topology cut
Sustainable directional capacity usable across it

gpu-chiplet-locality.text: Transfer demand across a chiplet topology cut takes at least crossing bytes divided by usable cut bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Rows in the left matrix and output
Columns in the right matrix and output
Reduction dimension shared by the inputs

systolic-array-dataflow.text: Dense matrix multiplication takes approximately two times output rows times output columns times reduction width floating-point operations.

aws-neuron-dataflow.text: Step time is at least the largest resource-time requirement among tensor, vector and transfer engines.

variables.meaning: Time-based service cost per accepted result
Charged service cost rate over the full accounting interval
Operational availability fraction over that interval

inference-custom-silicon.text: Cost per accepted result is the charged cost rate divided by the running accepted-result rate times operational availability.
inference-custom-silicon.note: a explicitly names the source availability term. Cost and result rates must use the same accounting interval and service target.

fpga-dsp-pipelines.text: Pipeline throughput is bounded by clock cycles per second divided by initiation cycles per item.

variables.meaning: Baseline time fraction offloaded and accelerated

dpu-infrastructure-offload.text: Overall offload speedup is the reciprocal of unchanged time fraction plus accelerated fraction divided by its speedup.

variables.meaning: Usable capacity of local storage region i
Payload bytes crossing the external boundary

wafer-scale-routing.text: Total local capacity sums the storage regions. External transfer time is at least external payload divided by sustainable external bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Programmed conductance from input i to output j

analog-photonic-research.text: In the ideal conductance-array model, each output current sums input voltage times its corresponding conductance.
analog-photonic-research.note: This electrical conductance equation models an analog crossbar mechanism; it is not a universal equation for every photonic architecture.

variables.meaning: Arrival rate of workload class k

chip-workload-contract.text: Aggregate resource demand sums each workload class’s request rate times its per-request demand.
chip-workload-contract.note: Choose one resource and unit before summing; bytes and operations cannot be added together.

variables.meaning: Possible configurations of b independent state bits

chip-rtl-verification.text: The configuration space of b independent binary state bits contains two to the power b states.

variables.meaning: Available setup timing margin on the selected path
Cell delay contribution on that path
Extracted wire delay contribution on that path

chip-physical-closure.text: Setup slack is the path’s available timing budget minus its cell and wire delays.

chip-tapeout-productization.text: A product is ready for the defined release only when every required acceptance gate has supporting evidence. Missing or failed gates keep that release unready; gate completion is not a percentage of nominal progress.
chip-tapeout-productization.note: The source logical-AND expression is a conceptual release checklist. No numeric gate value, universal gate set or probability of success is implied.

variables.meaning: Positive recurring saving per equivalent useful unit

chip-volume-economics.text: Break-even volume is additional fixed development cost divided by positive recurring savings per equivalent useful unit.
chip-volume-economics.note: The expression requires Δc > 0 and equal useful output/lifetime boundaries; it excludes unmodeled timing, risk and financing.

variables.meaning: Transfer time demanded at memory boundary j
Sustainable useful bandwidth at that boundary

memory-hierarchy-route.text: At each memory boundary, transfer demand takes at least crossing bytes divided by sustainable useful bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Effective bit rate per active data pin

memory-interface-choice.text: Raw interface bandwidth is active pin count times effective bit rate per pin divided by eight.

variables.meaning: Attainable throughput in the specified operation format
Useful bandwidth at the selected memory boundary
Useful operations per byte crossing that boundary

memory-wall-trends.text: Attainable throughput cannot exceed the smaller of arithmetic peak and bandwidth times arithmetic intensity.

graph-tensor-ir.text: Dense logical tensor size is bytes per element times the product of all dimension extents.

variables.meaning: Byte address of the element at logical indices i,j
Byte address of the logical origin
Element offset per one-index step on each axis

compiler-layout-lowering.text: The element’s byte address is base address plus bytes per element times the sum of each logical index times its element stride.

variables.meaning: Traffic avoided by removing one materialized intermediate write and read

kernel-locality-fusion.text: Avoided intermediate traffic is twice element count times bytes per element: one eliminated write and one eliminated read.

variables.meaning: Other unavoidable serial work, excluding those launch costs

runtime-device-dispatch.text: Total time is at least nonoverlapped launch count times launch overhead plus other unavoidable serial work.

variables.meaning: Combined occupancy at the chosen peak instant and device boundary
Resident weight storage at that instant
Resident gradient storage at that instant
Resident optimizer state at that instant

training-memory-state.text: Peak memory is the sum of weights, gradients, optimizer state, live activations and workspace at the same device boundary and the same instant.
training-memory-state.note: Do not add independently occurring category maxima as though they were simultaneous.

prefill-resource-trace.text: A dense projection uses approximately two times token positions times input width times output width floating-point operations.

variables.meaning: Decode-step time lower bound from weight traffic
Weight bytes actually read during the step

decode-bandwidth-trace.text: Decode-step time is at least actually read weight bytes divided by sustainable memory bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Dense score-matrix payload for one head and request

attention-io-tiling.text: A materialized dense score matrix contains query positions times key positions times bytes per score.

variables.meaning: Fraction of expert dispatches crossing the selected boundary

expert-routing-budget.text: Remote dispatch bytes equal tokens times experts per token times activation width times bytes per element times the remote-dispatch fraction.

variables.meaning: Payload transferred by the chosen algorithm at its boundary

parallelism-communication-budget.text: Communication time is approximately the phase count times startup latency plus transferred bytes divided by effective bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Useful bandwidth of the handoff path

disaggregated-serving.text: KV handoff takes at least transferred KV bytes divided by useful path bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Usable link payload rate in the stated direction

die-link-compatibility.text: Usable directional link rate is lane count times effective per-lane bit rate times payload efficiency divided by eight.

variables.meaning: Mean access latency in the two-tier model
Fraction of accesses using the near tier

pcie-cxl-semantics.text: Average latency weights the near and far access latencies by their respective access fractions.

interface-signal-eye.text: Unit interval is the reciprocal of symbol rate.
interface-signal-eye.note: A symbol can encode more than one bit; use symbol rate rather than payload bit rate here.

variables.meaning: Voltage excursion under the selected current/path sign convention

power-integrity-budget.text: First-order voltage excursion combines current times resistance with inductance times current slew rate.

variables.meaning: GPU count within the chosen assembly boundary

rack-reference-anatomy.text: Total GPU count is the number of trays times GPUs per tray.

variables.meaning: Time lower bound associated with the topology cut
Sustainable aggregate bandwidth actually usable across it

scaleup-scaleout-boundaries.text: Cut-crossing traffic requires at least its byte count divided by usable cut bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Effective one-direction payload bandwidth per rank

fabric-collective-traffic.text: Ideal ring duration is two times ranks minus one startup costs, plus two times ranks minus one divided by ranks times per-rank payload divided by bandwidth.

variables.meaning: Transmitted optical power relative to 1 mW
Receiver required input power at the stated criterion

optical-cpo-placement.text: Optical margin in decibels is transmit power in dBm minus path loss in dB minus required receive power in dBm.
optical-cpo-placement.note: These are logarithmic power quantities; do not insert linear watts into this subtraction.

variables.meaning: Real power entering the conversion stage
Current at the selected DC boundary
Power at that same DC boundary

rack-power-conversion.text: Output power equals conversion efficiency times input power. At the selected DC boundary, current is power divided by voltage.

variables.meaning: Energy consumed over the selected interval
Time-varying real power at the fixed metering boundary

rack-dynamic-power.text: Energy is the integral of power over time at a fixed metering boundary.
rack-dynamic-power.note: With watts and seconds the result is joules; this card uses MW and hours to obtain MWh.

variables.meaning: Heat transported by the selected single-phase stream

coolant-loop-separation.text: Single-phase transported heat is mass flow times specific heat times stream temperature rise.

variables.meaning: Cooling coefficient of performance at the declared point
Heat removed inside the stated cooling boundary
Electrical input included in that same cooling definition

facility-heat-rejection.text: Cooling COP is heat removed divided by the included electrical input power.

variables.meaning: Energy usable at the declared load-side boundary

grid-interconnection-readiness.text: Backup duration is already-usable energy divided by constant load power.
grid-interconnection-readiness.note: This load-side energy convention differs from a stored-energy input that still needs conversion efficiency.

cluster-commissioning-gates.text: A cluster is ready for the stated scope and date only when its electrical, thermal, fabric, software and operations acceptance conditions all have supporting evidence. Each condition is a gate, not a percentage of readiness.
cluster-commissioning-gates.note: This preserves the source Boolean conjunction as an operational checklist; additional product-specific gates can still be required.

variables.meaning: Complete products supportable from the coavailable inputs
Positive input-i requirement per finished product

compatible-supply-capacity.text: Complete products cannot exceed the smallest whole-number input count after each compatible supply is divided by its per-product requirement.

variables.meaning: Inventory at the beginning of discrete interval t
Inventory at the end of that interval

production-ramp-allocation.text: Next inventory equals current inventory plus arrivals minus consumption during the same interval.
production-ramp-allocation.note: A and C explicitly name the original arrivals and consumption functions; they are counts per interval, not unintegrated rates.

topology-job-admission.text: An allocation is feasible only when the job simultaneously meets its resource-count, memory, compatibility, topology and policy constraints. Each check applies to the same requested allocation.
topology-job-admission.note: The source conjunction describes a pedagogical admission checklist. It is not a scalar utilization score or a complete real scheduler.

variables.meaning: Approximate fractional loss of useful work time
System interruption rate in the rare-failure model

checkpoint-retained-work.text: Approximate loss fraction adds checkpoint cost per interval, expected half-interval lost work per failure, and recovery time per failure.
checkpoint-retained-work.note: The rare-failure approximation is not meaningful as an operating prediction when calculated overhead approaches or exceeds one.

variables.meaning: Storage service converted to the same useful sample basis
Transfer-stage service on that sample basis

storage-input-checkpoint-path.text: Useful input-pipeline rate cannot exceed the smallest storage, decoding, preparation or transfer rate after all use the same sample denominator.

variables.meaning: Compatible capacity with selected status s at time t
Capacity of nonoverlapping phase p at time t
Source-reported categorical status of phase p
Indicator: one when the stated status matches, zero otherwise

capacity-phase-geography.text: Status-scoped capacity sums each nonoverlapping phase’s compatible capacity only when its status matches the selected category.
capacity-phase-geography.note: The subscript s replaces the repeated word status to distinguish a selected category from the phase’s status function. Unknown capacity is not silently treated as zero.

variables.meaning: Average real power over that same interval and boundary

energy-forecast-boundaries.text: Energy is average power times the duration over which that average applies.
energy-forecast-boundaries.note: GW times hours gives GWh; divide GWh by 1000 for TWh. Installed peak power is not an interval-average load.

variables.meaning: Consumption-based water-use effectiveness for the chosen scope
Water consumed within that stated scope and interval
IT energy over the same interval

water-boundary-accounting.text: Consumption-based WUE is liters of water consumed divided by IT kilowatt-hours over the same interval.

variables.meaning: Declared preference weight for criterion i
Normalized metric value under the stated transformation

regional-siting-access.text: The scenario score sums normalized criterion values multiplied by declared preference weights.
regional-siting-access.note: This is a preference-dependent decision aid, not an objective scientific ranking. Weight normalization is a chosen convention, not implied by the sum.

orbital-evidence-status.text: Orbital compute service is ready for a specified workload and operating envelope only when compute, energy, thermal rejection, links, reliability and operations are all supported within that same envelope.
orbital-evidence-status.note: The source logical conjunction is a conceptual feasibility checklist, not a certification or a prediction of commercial viability.

variables.meaning: Incident solar irradiance at the selected condition

orbital-solar-storage.text: Instantaneous solar electrical power equals irradiance times active area times conversion efficiency times the orientation/degradation factor.

variables.meaning: Net heat-rejection rate under the declared sink/environment convention
Additional absorbed environmental heat not already represented by T_s

orbital-radiator-budget.text: Net heat rejection is emissivity times Stefan–Boltzmann constant times emitting area times radiator temperature to the fourth minus sink temperature to the fourth, less separately counted absorbed heat.
orbital-radiator-budget.note: Use kelvin in the fourth powers. Avoid double-counting environmental radiation in both the effective sink term and additional absorbed heat.

variables.meaning: One-way propagation time for the selected path
Speed of light along the modeled free-space path

orbital-link-contacts.text: Contact payload is bounded by efficiency times bit rate times contact duration divided by eight. One-way propagation time is path length divided by light speed.

variables.meaning: Expected radiation-event count in the modeled population

orbital-radiation-recovery.text: Expected event count is device count times per-device event rate times exposure duration.
orbital-radiation-recovery.note: Other time units are valid only if λ and t use the same unit.

variables.meaning: Fleet mass under the selected payload-specific mass model

orbital-replacement-mass.text: Fleet mass equals payload power capacity times mass per payload kilowatt. Steady replacement flow is approximately fleet mass divided by useful lifetime.
orbital-replacement-mass.note: A rate symbol replaces the original Mreplace/year label; this is a mass flow rather than another total mass.

variables.meaning: Launch-only cost annualized per payload kilowatt
Launch price per delivered kilogram under the selected scope
Useful operating life for the annualization

orbital-lifecycle-economics.text: Launch-only annualized cost per payload kilowatt is launch price per kilogram times mass per kilowatt divided by useful years.

crg-problem-statement.text: A physical-realization contract records five kinds of information: representation, interfaces, budgets, error model and verification evidence. Each must be instantiated for the chosen workload and physical boundary.
crg-problem-statement.note: The source tuple C_physical = (R, I, B, E, V) is a conceptual design scaffold. Its fields have different types and units, so the tuple is not a scalar physical equation or a theorem of realization.

variables.meaning: Bits transferred at the defined edge boundary
Effective bit-transfer bandwidth at that boundary
Modeled energy associated with those transferred bits
Effective energy per transferred bit under the stated convention

crg-communication-graph.text: Edge time is startup latency plus transferred bits divided by effective bit bandwidth. Edge energy is transferred bits times effective joules per bit.
crg-communication-graph.note: M is bits in both relations. If a payload is given in bytes, convert it before combining it with bit bandwidth or joules per bit; the energy term omits any separately unaccounted startup energy.

variables.meaning: Compatible arithmetic/work rate under the declared operation convention
Arithmetic capacity in that same convention
Useful operations per byte crossing the memory boundary
Useful operations per byte crossing the network boundary

crg-architecture-contract.text: Compatible work rate is bounded by the smallest arithmetic, memory-delivery and network-delivery rate after each is expressed on the same operation basis.
crg-architecture-contract.note: If the desired output is tasks/s rather than operations/s, normalize all three bounds by the same declared operations per task before comparison.

variables.meaning: Launch register clock-to-Q delay for the selected analysis

crg-chip-design-realization.text: The clock period must cover clock-to-Q, logic, setup and uncertainty terms for the specified timing path.

variables.meaning: Accepted retained work at the declared task boundary
Executed work before the modeled acceptance/retention reductions
Quality/acceptance fraction under the declared conditional or separable accounting
Fraction of executed work lost to the modeled interruptions/recovery

crg-package-system-closure.text: Useful work is executed work times its declared acceptance fraction times the fraction retained after modeled losses.
crg-package-system-closure.note: The two factors require a conditional or otherwise justified separable accounting convention. Do not assume independent quality and interruption outcomes or double-count rejected work. W here denotes work quantity, not watts.

crg-55-year-resolution.text: A research claim, the evidence offered to support it, and an operational qualification decision are distinct record types. Keeping them separate preserves what has been asserted, what has been observed and what has been accepted for a specific use.
crg-55-year-resolution.note: The source claim ≠ evidence ≠ qualification is an epistemic distinction, not a numerical inequality or a judgment of the research claim’s ultimate correctness.

variables.meaning: Margin above a minimum required value
variables.unit: same units as the selected metric

variables.meaning: Observed metric at the declared configuration and time
Minimum acceptable value in the same metric and units

crg-verification-loop.text: For a minimum requirement, margin is observed value minus the required value; a negative margin fails that minimum.
crg-verification-loop.note: This subtraction convention applies to lower-bound requirements such as minimum throughput. For an upper limit such as maximum temperature, positive headroom instead uses limit minus observed. The original generic failure statement needs this direction qualification.
